options: A Java library added to a regular application — not a separate cluster or service
A standalone cluster that runs alongside Kafka brokers, like Flink or Spark
A configuration file format for Kafka Connect
A GUI tool for browsing topics
questions.explain: Unlike Flink or Spark Structured Streaming, a Kafka Streams app is just a JVM process using ordinary consumer and producer clients.

questions.q: How does a Kafka Streams application scale out to handle more load?
options: Run more instances of the same application — Kafka's consumer group protocol divides the input topic's partitions across them
It cannot scale beyond a single instance
By manually editing ZooKeeper configuration
By converting the topology into a Kafka Connect connector
questions.explain: Kafka Streams reuses the same consumer group mechanics covered in Lesson 8 — no separate scheduler is needed.

questions.q: What distinguishes a stateful operation like a running count per customer from a stateless one like filter?
options: A stateful operation needs to remember something across events, and Kafka Streams keeps that in a local state store backed by a changelog topic
Stateful operations never write any output
Stateless operations require more memory than stateful ones
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: The changelog topic lets the state store be rebuilt if an instance fails — it isn't just kept in memory and lost.

questions.q: In the example topology, what does the filter step do before the mapValues step?
options: Keeps only orders with an amount over 100, discarding the rest before further processing
Deletes the orders topic entirely
Groups all orders by customer ID
Writes every order directly to high-value-orders unfiltered
questions.explain: filter((key, order) -> order.getAmount() > 100) removes orders at or below that threshold before mapValues tags the survivors.

questions.q: How does Kafka Streams relate to Kafka Connect and ksqlDB, per this lesson?
options: Connect moves data without code, Streams is full application code against a topic, and ksqlDB sits in between with SQL syntax over the same engine
They are three unrelated products from different vendors
Kafka Streams replaces the need for Kafka Connect entirely
ksqlDB is a replacement for Kafka's consumer group protocol
questions.explain: All three solve different points on the same spectrum: no-code movement, full code, or SQL over Kafka topics.
